Indian equity indices ended lower for the fourth consecutive session on September 3, giving up early gains as buying in media, realty and banking stocks was outweighed by selling in auto, IT and pharma names.

The markets opened higher amid positive global cues and softer crude oil prices, with the Nifty reclaiming the 24,000 mark in early trade. However, gains failed to sustain as the session progressed, with profit-taking dragging the index below 23,900 after the Closing Auction Session (CAS).
At close, the Sensex was down 417.49 points or 0.55 percent at 76,152.86, and the Nifty was down 41 points or 0.17 percent at 23,873.45.
The broader market outperformed the main indices, with the Nifty Midcap index rising 0.37 percent and the smallcap index advancing 1.2 percent.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Up)
GIFT Nifty was trading with a gain of 90 points at around 24,023 in early trade, indicating a positive opening for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Equities (Up)
Asian stocks rose as investors pared bets on a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike this month, weakening the dollar.

MSCI’s Asia Pacific equities gauge climbed 0.3%, led by technology stocks in South Korea, after Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he would support keeping rates steady if price pressures continued to ease. His comments had earlier fueled gains on Wall Street as swaps priced roughly even odds of a quarter-point hike in September, down from about 70% earlier this week.
US Equities (Rise)

Wall Street rallied on Thursday as investors curbed their rate hike bets after U.S. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he would support holding the Fed funds target rate steady if data shows inflationary pressures are abating.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 624.16 points, or 1.18%, to 53,686.11; the S&P 500 gained 81.11 points, or 1.06%, to 7,747.71 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 366.23 points, or 1.40%, to 26,584.06.
Dollar Index (Down)
The dollar sank to the lowest level since May after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller noted progress on inflation and as the yen surged against its major counterparts.
US Bond Yield (Flat)
The yields on 10-year Treasuries and 2-year Treasuries were little changed at 4.76% and 4.33%, respectively.
Asian Currencies (Up)

Asian currencies were largely positive against the US dollar, with the Indonesian rupiah (+0.475%) emerging as the strongest gainer, followed by the Taiwan dollar (+0.202%) and South Korean won (-0.158%)? Correction: the won was the only notable decliner along with the ringgit. Specifically, the South Korean won (-0.158%) and Malaysian ringgit (-0.007%) weakened, while the Japanese yen (+0.026%), Thai baht (+0.030%), Chinese renminbi (+0.037%), Singapore dollar (+0.008%), and Philippine peso (+0.122%) edged higher.
Crude (Up)
Oil prices rose on Friday and are on track for the steepest weekly gain since mid-July as rising tensions and renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities heightened concerns over Middle East supply risks.
Gold (Flat)

Gold steadied — after rising more than 2% on Thursday — after a Federal Reserve official’s comments on inflation helped to lower the odds of an interest-rate hike. Spot bullion was trading around $4,480 an ounce and was poised to eke out a modest weekly gain after dropping sharply on Tuesday before rebounding.
Fund Flow Action

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) sold equities worth Rs 2,345 crore in the Indian equity market on September 3, while domestic institutional investors (DIIs) bought equities worth Rs 4,977 crore.
